title: Design a distributed cache
prompt: You're building a distributed in-memory cache (think Redis/Memcached cluster) to absorb read-heavy traffic from a backing database. The dominant forcing constraint is horizontal key distribution: a single cache box can't hold the working set or serve the QPS, so keys must be spread across many cache nodes via a coordinator doing consistent hashing — and adding/removing a node must reshuffle only a small slice of keys, not the whole space. Draw the path from a client, through a cache-coordinator service (or balancer) that routes each key to the right shard, across the cache nodes, and back to the source-of-truth database for cache-aside/write-through on a miss. Show how routing, sharding, and the backing store fit together.

criteria.label: Request originates from a client
criteria.metWhy: Good — the cache request starts from a client/user.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client component as the entry point that issues GET/SET requests to the cache.

criteria.label: A coordinator routes keys via consistent hashing
criteria.metWhy: Strong — a coordinator/router tier sits in front of the shards to place each key.
criteria.why: Add a Server (or Load Balancer / API Gateway) acting as the cache coordinator that hashes each key to a shard. Without it, no consistent-hashing layer decides which node owns a key.

criteria.label: Cache nodes hold the partitioned data
criteria.metWhy: Core — the in-memory cache tier (shards) holds the working set.
criteria.why: Add a Cache component (the cache nodes/shards). This is the heart of a distributed cache — the in-memory store that absorbs reads.

criteria.label: A durable database is the source of truth
criteria.metWhy: Good — a durable backing store is the source of truth behind the cache.
criteria.why: Add a Database as the backing source of truth. Cache-aside/write-through needs a durable store to fill from on a miss and persist writes.

criteria.label: Coordinator routes requests to the cache nodes
criteria.metWhy: Strong — the coordinator is wired to the shards, so keys reach the right node.
criteria.why: Connect the coordinator (Server/Balancer/API Gateway) to the Cache nodes so hashed keys are routed to their owning shard.

criteria.label: Service falls back to the database on a miss
criteria.metWhy: Good — a cache miss falls back to the durable store to refill.
criteria.why: Connect the service (or cache tier) to the Database so a miss reads through to the source of truth and repopulates the cache.

criteria.label: Client reaches the cache through the coordinator
criteria.metWhy: Good — client traffic enters through the routing/coordinator tier.
criteria.why: Connect the User/Client to the coordinator (Server/Balancer/API Gateway) so requests enter through the routing layer rather than hitting shards directly.

criteria.label: Monitoring tracks hit-rate and node health
criteria.metWhy: Nice — monitoring surfaces hit-rate, evictions, and node failures.
criteria.why: Add a Monitoring component to track cache hit-rate, eviction, latency, and node health so you can detect a hot shard or a failed node.
